proposals.clause_text: Watch (b): Settlement with no admission of wrongdoing
proposals.summary: Ford agreed to pay $2.3 million under an EEOC conciliation agreement resolving a 2021 charge of race and national-origin harassment at its Buffalo stamping plant. The EEOC's investigation found reasonable cause to believe the harassment occurred.
proposals.caveat: The EEOC release does not mention an admission, and the conciliation agreement itself was not reviewed, so "no admission" is not confirmed. Same open question as Tesla: does an EEOC "reasonable cause" finding count as an "agency finding" under the Black rule? This screen treats it as NOT qualifying until the team decides.
proposals.tripwire: Team rules that EEOC cause findings qualify, or a court/agency adjudicates a violation -> propose Black under (b).

evidence.publisher: U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (press release)
evidence.quote: The EEOC's investigation found reasonable cause to believe that Ford personnel at the facility subjected numerous employees to harassment and discrimination based on race and national origin.

evidence.publisher: U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (press release)
evidence.quote: Following the EEOC's investigation, the parties engaged in the EEOC's pre-litigation conciliation process, resulting in a conciliation agreement.

proposals.clause_text: Watch (b): Settlement with no admission of wrongdoing
proposals.summary: Accenture agreed to pay $25 million to resolve DOJ False Claims Act allegations that its federal-services unit certified non-discrimination in federal contracts while taking race or sex into account in employment decisions. DOJ states the claims are allegations only.
proposals.tripwire: A court ruling, jury verdict, or agency finding that Accenture engaged in racial discrimination -> propose Black under (b).

evidence.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Public Affairs (press release)
evidence.quote: to resolve alleged violations of the False Claims Act for failing to comply with anti-discrimination requirements in federal contracts and discriminating against employees and applicants for employment because of race or sex.

evidence.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Public Affairs (press release)
evidence.quote: The claims resolved by the United States in the settlement are allegations only and there has been no determination of liability.

proposals.clause_text: Black (c) At least 10% of latest fiscal-year revenue comes from immigration detention, or immigration detainee monitoring or transport, as disclosed in the company's own 10-K: 35% of fiscal-year 2025 revenue (10-K filed 2026-02-20; threshold 10%)
proposals.summary: CoreCivic's 10-K for fiscal 2025 states that ICE accounted for 35% ($770.7 million) of its total revenue (29% in 2024, 30% in 2023).
proposals.caveat: The 10-K gives ICE's share of total revenue, not a separate "immigration detention" line. This screen treats ICE contract revenue as the clause (c) measure, as in the rule's own example. The 10-K does not split ICE revenue between detention and any other service; the team may want to confirm that reading.

evidence.publisher: CoreCivic, Inc. Form 10-K for fiscal year 2025 (SEC EDGAR)
evidence.quote: For the year ended December 31, 2025, ICE, USMS, and the BOP accounted for 35% ($770.7 million), 18% ($390.6 million), and 1% ($32.2 million), respectively, of our total revenue.

proposals.clause_text: Black (c) At least 10% of latest fiscal-year revenue comes from immigration detention, or immigration detainee monitoring or transport, as disclosed in the company's own 10-K: 47.6% of fiscal-year 2025 revenue (10-K filed 2026-02-25; threshold 10%)
proposals.summary: GEO Group's 10-K for fiscal 2025 states that ICE accounted for 47.6% of its total consolidated revenues (41.5% in 2024).
proposals.caveat: The 10-K gives ICE's share of total consolidated revenues, not a separate "immigration detention" line. This screen treats ICE contract revenue as the clause (c) measure, as in the rule's own example. GEO's ICE revenue includes an electronic-monitoring contract (ISAP) as well as detention; both fall under clause (c).

evidence.publisher: The GEO Group, Inc. Form 10-K for fiscal year 2025 (SEC EDGAR)
evidence.quote: ICE accounting for 47.6% and 41.5% of our total consolidated revenues for 2025 and 2024, respectively

proposals.clause_text: Watch (b): Settlement with no admission of wrongdoing
proposals.summary: PayPal agreed to a DOJ settlement resolving a fair lending investigation into an investment program for Black and minority-owned businesses, valued at about $30 million in fee waivers.
proposals.caveat: The DOJ release does not say whether PayPal admitted wrongdoing, so "no admission" is not confirmed; the settlement agreement itself was not reviewed. DOJ describes the program as discriminatory on race and national origin; no court or agency ruling is cited.
proposals.tripwire: A court ruling, jury verdict, or agency finding or consent order that states PayPal discriminated, or an admission in the settlement -> propose Black under (b).

evidence.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Public Affairs (press release)
evidence.quote: the Justice Department announced a settlement with PayPal Inc. to resolve a fair lending investigation into a discriminatory investment program created for black and minority-owned businesses.

proposals.caveat: The EEOC release does not say whether Cardinal Health admitted wrongdoing, so "no admission" is not confirmed; the consent decree was not reviewed. The release is dated 2021-07-09 (inside the 7-year window until 2028-07-09).
proposals.tripwire: A court ruling, jury verdict, or agency finding that states a violation, or an admission in the decree -> propose Black under (b).

evidence.publisher: U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (press release)
evidence.quote: Cardinal Health will pay $1.45 million to resolve a racial harassment and retaliation discrimination lawsuit filed by the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC)

proposals.clause_text: Watch (b): Settlement with no admission of wrongdoing

proposals.clause_text: Watch (b): Settlement with no admission of wrongdoing
proposals.summary: Dollar General agreed to pay $6 million under a consent decree settling an EEOC class lawsuit alleging its criminal-background-check screen discriminated against African American applicants (a disparate-impact claim). The allegations are the EEOC's.
proposals.caveat: The EEOC release does not say whether Dollar General admitted wrongdoing, so "no admission" is not confirmed. The three-year decree has ended. The release is dated 2019-11-18, which leaves the 7-year window on 2026-11-18, after which this record would no longer apply.
proposals.tripwire: A court ruling, jury verdict, or agency finding that states a violation, or an admission in the decree -> propose Black under (b).

evidence.publisher: U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (press release)
evidence.quote: Dollar General will pay $6 million and furnish other relief to settle a class race discrimination lawsuit brought by the U.S. Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC)

proposals.clause_text: Black (a) Knowingly spread false information to the public: Court ruling on the merits (including summary judgment on falsity), 2023-03-31 (within 7 years). Scope: court found the statements false; knowledge (actual malice) was not adjudicated
proposals.summary: Delaware Superior Court granted Dominion summary judgment on falsity: Fox News statements about Dominion and the 2020 election were false. Fox Corp and Fox News Network settled on April 18, 2023 (about $800M including a related suit, per Fox's filing).
proposals.caveat: The court decided falsity only. Actual malice (the "knowingly" part) was left for trial and never decided because the case settled. The team's rule lists summary judgment on falsity as a qualifying finding, so this is proposed; the team should confirm it accepts a falsity finding for clause (a). The ruling names Fox News Network, LLC, a Fox Corp subsidiary.

evidence.publisher: Superior Court of the State of Delaware (C.A. No. N21C-03-257 EMD)
evidence.quote: The evidence developed in this civil proceeding demonstrates that is CRYSTAL clear that none of the Statements relating to Dominion about the 2020 election are true. Therefore, the Court will grant summary judgment in favor of Dominion on the element of falsity.

evidence.publisher: Fox Corporation Form 10-Q (SEC EDGAR)
evidence.quote: On March 31, 2023, the court in the Dominion case issued its rulings on summary judgment motions that were unfavorable to the Company. Following these rulings, on April 18, 2023, the Company and its subsidiary, Fox News Network, LLC, entered into a Release and Settlement Agreement with Dominion

proposals.clause_text: Black (a) Knowingly spread false information to the public: Court ruling on the merits (including summary judgment on falsity), 2025-04-09 (within 7 years). Scope: court found the statements false; knowledge (actual malice) was not adjudicated
proposals.summary: Delaware Superior Court granted Dominion summary judgment that Newsmax's statements were defamatory per se and false. Newsmax settled with Dominion for $67M on August 15, 2025.
proposals.caveat: Actual malice and damages were left for trial and never decided because the case settled. The ruling names Newsmax Media, Inc. and Newsmax Broadcasting, LLC; Newsmax Inc. (NMAX) is their parent and reported the settlement in its own 8-K.

evidence.publisher: Superior Court of the State of Delaware (C.A. No. N21C-08-063 EMD)
evidence.quote: Newsmax fails to meet its rebuttal burden of showing that an issue of material fact exists as to falsity. Therefore, the Court GRANTS summary judgment in Dominion's favor regarding falsity.

evidence.publisher: Newsmax Inc. Form 8-K (SEC EDGAR)
evidence.quote: On August 15, 2025, Newsmax Media, Inc. and Newsmax Broadcasting, LLC entered into a settlement agreement with Dominion Voting Systems, Inc. and certain of its affiliates ("Dominion"), pursuant to which such parties agreed to resolve the lawsuit among them for a total amount of $67 million

proposals.clause_text: Black (b) Engaged in discrimination on the basis of race, ethnicity, sexual orientation or gender identity: Jury verdict, even if later reduced, 2021-10-04 (within 7 years)
proposals.summary: A federal jury (N.D. Cal., Diaz v. Tesla) returned a verdict against Tesla on a former contingent worker's race-discrimination claims at the Fremont factory. Damages were later reduced ($136.9M to $15M to $3.175M after a retrial); the parties settled confidentially in March 2024.
proposals.caveat: NEW vs. the September starting list, which had TSLA on Watch. The rule counts "a jury verdict, even if later reduced", and October 2021 is inside the 7-year window (until 2028-10-04). The worker was a contingent (staffing-agency) worker. This is a proposal for the team to decide.

evidence.publisher: Tesla, Inc. Form 10-Q (SEC EDGAR)
evidence.quote: On October 4, 2021, in a case captioned Diaz v. Tesla, a jury in the Northern District of California returned a verdict against Tesla on claims by a former contingent worker that he was subjected to race discrimination

evidence.publisher: Tesla, Inc. Form 10-Q (SEC EDGAR)
evidence.quote: the damages awarded against Tesla were reduced from an initial $ 136.9 million (October 4, 2021) down to $ 15 million (April 13, 2022), and then further down to $ 3.175 million (April 3, 2023).

proposals.clause_text: Watch (b): Open lawsuit or agency complaint on (a) or (b) that has survived a motion to dismiss
proposals.summary: California Civil Rights Department suit (filed Feb 9, 2022) alleging systemic race discrimination at Fremont; first trial phase set for Sept 21, 2026. Separate EEOC suit (filed Sept 28, 2023) for race harassment and retaliation is in discovery. EEOC issued a cause finding on June 1, 2022.
proposals.caveat: Both suits are past the pleading stage (one set for trial, one in discovery). The 10-Q does not mention a motion to dismiss; "survived" is inferred from the trial setting and discovery. Whether the CRD trial actually began on Sept 21, 2026 was not confirmed from a primary source this run (calcivilrights.ca.gov refused scripted access). Open question for the team: does an EEOC "cause finding" count as an "agency finding" under the Black rule? This screen treats it as NOT qualifying until the team decides, because it is a preliminary determination, not an adjudication.
proposals.tripwire: A liability finding in the CRD trial or in EEOC v. Tesla (N.D. Cal.) -> propose Black under (b). If the Diaz proposal is approved, TSLA is already Black and this becomes context.

evidence.publisher: Tesla, Inc. Form 10-Q (SEC EDGAR)
evidence.quote: on February 9, 2022, the California Civil Rights Department ("CRD," formerly "DFEH") filed a civil complaint against Tesla in Alameda County, California Superior Court, alleging systemic race discrimination, hostile work environment and pay equity claims, among others.

evidence.publisher: Tesla, Inc. Form 10-Q (SEC EDGAR)
evidence.quote: The first phase of the trial is currently set for September 21, 2026. Additionally, on June 1, 2022, the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission ("EEOC") issued a cause finding against Tesla that closely parallels the CRD's allegations.

proposals.clause_text: Watch (b): Settlement with no admission of wrongdoing
proposals.summary: DOJ sued Meta (S.D.N.Y., June 21, 2022) alleging its housing-ad delivery system discriminated by race and other traits under the Fair Housing Act; settled the same month with no admission and no finding of liability. Court approved it June 27, 2022.
proposals.caveat: The underlying HUD Charge of Discrimination (March 28, 2019) followed a "reasonable cause" determination; that is now older than 7 years and is a charge, not an adjudication.
proposals.tripwire: A new adjudicated finding (court ruling, jury verdict, or agency finding stating a violation) that Meta engaged in (a) or (b) -> propose Black.

evidence.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Rights Division (settlement agreement, 22 Civ. 5187)
evidence.quote: this Settlement Agreement is for settlement purposes only and does not constitute an admission by Meta of any of the allegations contained in the HUD Charge or the Complaint, nor does it constitute any finding of liability against Meta

evidence.publisher: U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Rights Division (case page)
evidence.quote: alleged that Meta's housing advertising system discriminated against Facebook users based on their race, color, religion, sex, disability, familial status, and national origin, in violation of the Fair Housing Act (FHA).

proposals.clause_text: Watch (a): Open lawsuit or agency complaint on (a) or (b) that has survived a motion to dismiss
proposals.summary: Multistate attorneys-general case (N.D. Cal.) alleging Meta misled the public about risks of Instagram and Facebook to young users. Trial began Aug 18, 2026; a settlement of up to $17.1B was announced Aug 26, 2026, subject to court approval.
proposals.caveat: The California AG release does not mention an admission. The settlement document itself was not reviewed this run, so "no admission" is not yet confirmed. Until the court approves it, this is treated as an open case under (a).
proposals.tripwire: If the approved settlement or a court order contains an admission or finding that Meta knowingly misled the public -> propose Black under (a). If approved with no admission -> Watch (settlement with no admission).

evidence.publisher: California Attorney General (press release)
evidence.quote: all the while misleading users, their families, and the public regarding the existence and severity of these risks. Trial in this case began on August 18 in the U.S. District Court for the Northern District of California.

evidence.publisher: California Attorney General (press release)
evidence.quote: Today's settlement, subject to court approval, provides for strong injunctive terms

evidence.publisher: U.S. Attorney's Office, N.D.N.Y. (statement, via DOJ press-release API)
evidence.quote: Today's announcement that Meta has agreed to pay up to $17.1 billion and implement reforms across Facebook and Instagram is an encouraging step forward.

records.summary: Ford agreed to pay $2.3 million under an EEOC conciliation agreement resolving a 2021 charge of race and national-origin harassment at its Buffalo stamping plant. The EEOC's investigation found reasonable cause to believe the harassment occurred.
records.caveat: The EEOC release does not mention an admission, and the conciliation agreement itself was not reviewed, so "no admission" is not confirmed. Same open question as Tesla: does an EEOC "reasonable cause" finding count as an "agency finding" under the Black rule? This screen treats it as NOT qualifying until the team decides.
records.tripwire: Team rules that EEOC cause findings qualify, or a court/agency adjudicates a violation -> propose Black under (b).

records.summary: Delaware Superior Court granted Dominion summary judgment on falsity: Fox News statements about Dominion and the 2020 election were false. Fox Corp and Fox News Network settled on April 18, 2023 (about $800M including a related suit, per Fox's filing).
records.caveat: The court decided falsity only. Actual malice (the "knowingly" part) was left for trial and never decided because the case settled. The team's rule lists summary judgment on falsity as a qualifying finding, so this is proposed; the team should confirm it accepts a falsity finding for clause (a). The ruling names Fox News Network, LLC, a Fox Corp subsidiary.

sources.publisher: Superior Court of the State of Delaware (C.A. No. N21C-03-257 EMD)
sources.quote: The evidence developed in this civil proceeding demonstrates that is CRYSTAL clear that none of the Statements relating to Dominion about the 2020 election are true. Therefore, the Court will grant summary judgment in favor of Dominion on the element of falsity.

sources.publisher: Fox Corporation Form 10-Q (SEC EDGAR)
sources.quote: On March 31, 2023, the court in the Dominion case issued its rulings on summary judgment motions that were unfavorable to the Company. Following these rulings, on April 18, 2023, the Company and its subsidiary, Fox News Network, LLC, entered into a Release and Settlement Agreement with Dominion

records.summary: A federal jury (N.D. Cal., Diaz v. Tesla) returned a verdict against Tesla on a former contingent worker's race-discrimination claims at the Fremont factory. Damages were later reduced ($136.9M to $15M to $3.175M after a retrial); the parties settled confidentially in March 2024.
records.caveat: NEW vs. the September starting list, which had TSLA on Watch. The rule counts "a jury verdict, even if later reduced", and October 2021 is inside the 7-year window (until 2028-10-04). The worker was a contingent (staffing-agency) worker. This is a proposal for the team to decide.

records.summary: California Civil Rights Department suit (filed Feb 9, 2022) alleging systemic race discrimination at Fremont; first trial phase set for Sept 21, 2026. Separate EEOC suit (filed Sept 28, 2023) for race harassment and retaliation is in discovery. EEOC issued a cause finding on June 1, 2022.
records.caveat: Both suits are past the pleading stage (one set for trial, one in discovery). The 10-Q does not mention a motion to dismiss; "survived" is inferred from the trial setting and discovery. Whether the CRD trial actually began on Sept 21, 2026 was not confirmed from a primary source this run (calcivilrights.ca.gov refused scripted access). Open question for the team: does an EEOC "cause finding" count as an "agency finding" under the Black rule? This screen treats it as NOT qualifying until the team decides, because it is a preliminary determination, not an adjudication.
records.tripwire: A liability finding in the CRD trial or in EEOC v. Tesla (N.D. Cal.) -> propose Black under (b). If the Diaz proposal is approved, TSLA is already Black and this becomes context.

records.summary: DOJ sued Meta (S.D.N.Y., June 21, 2022) alleging its housing-ad delivery system discriminated by race and other traits under the Fair Housing Act; settled the same month with no admission and no finding of liability. Court approved it June 27, 2022.
records.caveat: The underlying HUD Charge of Discrimination (March 28, 2019) followed a "reasonable cause" determination; that is now older than 7 years and is a charge, not an adjudication.

records.summary: Multistate attorneys-general case (N.D. Cal.) alleging Meta misled the public about risks of Instagram and Facebook to young users. Trial began Aug 18, 2026; a settlement of up to $17.1B was announced Aug 26, 2026, subject to court approval.
records.caveat: The California AG release does not mention an admission. The settlement document itself was not reviewed this run, so "no admission" is not yet confirmed. Until the court approves it, this is treated as an open case under (a).
records.tripwire: If the approved settlement or a court order contains an admission or finding that Meta knowingly misled the public -> propose Black under (a). If approved with no admission -> Watch (settlement with no admission).
